summary: You have a solid, consistent profile across your studies, with real strengths in your capstone work (Project Management, Industry Standards Application and Technical Communication all sitting near 78-80%). The two areas to focus on are foundational: Object-Oriented Design and Implementation (72.0%, flagged as an isolated gap) and Data Structures and Algorithms (73.4%, a persistent but stable gap across CSE1OOF and CSE2ALG). Markers across your OOF and ALG assessments consistently ask for the same next step: clearer reasoning, tighter technical precision, and more complete testing or reflection. Targeting exactly that should lift both gap areas.

priorities.evidence: This is your lowest area at 72.0% (CSE1OOF 72.2%) and is flagged as an isolated gap. Your CSE1OOF:Central examination (71.0%) and CSE1OOF:Test (71.0%) are your weakest OOF results, and markers repeatedly note the need for clearer reasoning, better technical precision and more complete testing or reflection.
priorities.actions: Revisit the marker feedback on CSE1OOF:Central examination and CSE1OOF:Test, then re-attempt design questions tied to CSE1OOF:SILO1 by writing out object models that combine data and behaviour before coding. Redo a CSE1OOF:Practical demonstration style exercise for CSE1OOF:SILO4, implementing a small real-life problem end to end and adding a full test suite. For CSE1OOF:SILO3, refactor an earlier CSE1OOF:Assignment solution to reuse and share code, documenting your reasoning at each step.

Re-implement searching and sorting algorithms in Java for CSE2ALG:SILO3 and add performance measurements to evaluate them per CSE2ALG:SILO5. Review CSE2ALG:Test feedback and re-practise identifying appropriate structures for given contexts (CSE2ALG:SILO2), and revisit encapsulation and abstract data types (CSE1OOF:SILO2) so your implementations localise change.
